steps.text: Remove the battery compartment door from the back of the Remote Control.
Install four AAA batteries, observing the polarity markings.
Replace the battery compartment door.

notes: As an RF-only device it needs at least one Access Point 2443 or other dual-band Insteon device; the manual recommends at least two.
Use alkaline or high-quality rechargeable batteries; a fresh alkaline set gives about 1,500 to 2,000 button taps.

steps.text: Choose the On/Off button pair (scene A to F) to use.
Press and hold the On button of that pair until the Remote Control beeps, about 10 seconds.

notes: Set the responder to the state you want first, then, after putting the Remote Control in linking mode, press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds. The Remote Control beeps and its status LED stops blinking and turns off.
Any accidental button press ends linking mode early.

steps.text: Press and hold the On button of the pair for 10 seconds to enter linking mode.
Tap the same On button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: While the device is still awake, have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
When done, tap the same On button to leave multi-linking mode.

notes: Put the device in linking mode before the Hub starts ALL-Linking. This links the device to the Hub as a controller, with the Hub as the responder, so the Hub receives the device's reports; the Hub makes no link to the device.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's multi-linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the On button of the pair for 10 seconds to enter linking mode.
Tap the same On button.
One at a time, press and hold each responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
When done, tap the same On button to leave multi-linking mode.

notes: Multi-linking mode times out after 4 minutes of inactivity.

The manual gives these steps for controllers in general ("if the controller does not have a SET button, tap the same On or Scene button") and does not list the Remote Control's beeps or LED for this mode.

verification.note: Read from the manual's generic multi-linking steps for controllers without a SET button.

steps.text: Press and hold the On button of the pair to unlink until the Remote Control beeps, about 10 seconds.
Press and hold the same On button again until it beeps, about 10 seconds.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds within 4 minutes. The Remote Control beeps and its status LED stops blinking and turns off.
Unlink responders you no longer use; otherwise the Remote Control keeps retrying commands and slows the system.

steps.text: Unlink any devices the Remote Control controls.
Remove one battery.
Wait at least 10 seconds.
While holding down the Bright button, reinsert the battery.
steps.expect: Beep; status LED turns on solid

steps.text: Keep holding the Bright button for about 10 seconds.
Release the Bright button.
steps.expect: Continuous beep while held; double beep and status LED turns off on release

notes: The factory reset clears all Insteon links.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Press and hold the On button of the pair to unlink until the Remote Control beeps, about 10 seconds.
Press and hold the same On button again until it beeps, about 10 seconds.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0.
steps.expect: The device deletes its link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
